title: Lesson 8: How to Disciple Others
description: Make space for one person, then send them to make space for someone else.

blocks.text: So far in Growing Out you have learned to pray for people, listen, serve, share your faith, and stand firm. Now it is time to help someone else grow.
Making Space

Someone made space for you. They answered your questions, prayed for you, or opened the Bible with you when you did not know where to start. Before any of them, Jesus made room for you at His table when you had nothing to bring. That is grace, and it comes first.
8.1 - Who made space for you as you learned to follow Jesus? What did they do that you still remember?

Now it is your turn. Making space means clearing an hour in your week and pulling out a chair for one person. Start with your three spaces from Lesson 6: home, work and school, and everywhere else. There is an open chair in each one. A coworker with questions. A neighbor who is new to faith. A teenager at your kitchen table.

blocks.title: Four Generations
blocks.text:
Paul met Timothy in Lystra, a young man the believers there spoke well of (Acts 16:1-2). Paul did not hand him a book and wish him well. He took Timothy with him. Timothy heard Paul teach, watched him pray, and saw how he handled hardship. Later the two of them wrote a letter together to a young church, saying, "we were ready to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves" (1 Thessalonians 2:8).

Near the end of his life, Paul gave Timothy this charge:
and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.
Count the generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others. People discipling people who disciple people. Paul sat with Timothy so that Timothy could one day sit with someone else.

Jesus did it first. He appointed twelve "so that they might be with him and he might send them out to preach" (Mark 3:14). First with Him, then sent. Tap through the drawing below and watch one table.
Make SPACES

Did you notice the camera pulling back? You may not have known why until the very end. The table was never the goal. The room was. Those steps spell SPACES: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage, Send. Jesus lived every one of them with His friends, and you can live them with one person.

Study. Jesus opened the Scriptures to two discouraged friends on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24:27). Open God's Word together, let a Growing Together lesson guide you, and ask what it means for this week.

Practice. Jesus sent the Twelve out two by two, and when they came back He listened to all they had done (Mark 6:7, 30). Let your friend try what they are learning with you first, like telling their story or explaining a passage.

Appropriate Challenge. After Peter denied Him, Jesus did not set him aside. He gave him a next step that fit: "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17). Offer one step that stretches without crushing, such as praying out loud or inviting a friend to church.

Encourage. Jesus told Peter, "I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail" (Luke 22:32). Ask how it went, listen, pray, and celebrate the courage it took. When it goes badly, stay close. Encouragement is how people find the nerve to try again.

Send. Jesus told His disciples, "As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you" (John 20:21), and He promised to be with them always (Matthew 28:20). When the time is right, say, "You are ready to sit down with someone else." Then pull out your chair for someone new.
8.2 - Which of your three spaces has an open chair in it right now? What would you need to move in your week to make room for one person?
Who Could You Sit With?

Paul told Timothy to look for faithful people. An easy way to remember what to look for is faithful, available, and teachable. They do not need to know much or look impressive. They need to want to grow and be willing to show up. Start with one person, not a program. Ask, "Would you like to go through a Bible study with me?" Meet once a week or every other week. A kitchen table, a break room, or a coffee shop is enough.

You may feel unqualified. So did the people Jesus first sent. You do not need every answer. You need to keep following Jesus, care about one person, and share what you are learning. The same Growing Together lessons that helped you can guide the conversation.
8.3 - Who is one faithful, available, and teachable person you could invite to sit down with you?
God Gives the Growth

Paul wrote, "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth" (1 Corinthians 3:6). You cannot change anyone's heart. You can make space, open the Word, practice together, give a fitting challenge, encourage, and send. Then you trust the Holy Spirit with the rest. Some tables will feel fruitful and some will feel slow. Keep showing up. The room in the drawing did not fill in a week, and it does not need to. It fills one table at a time.
8.4 - Picture the person you named one day pulling out a chair for someone else. What would you most want to have shared with them by then?
Lesson 8 Review

Someone made space for you, and Jesus made room for you first. Now you get to make space for someone else. Paul sat with Timothy so that Timothy could sit with others, and Jesus called His friends to be with Him and then sent them. Make SPACES: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage, Send. Start with one person at one table, and trust God to fill the room.
In the next lesson, you will consider the people God places beside you in His mission, from your church to the ends of the earth.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
Further reading: The Disciple Maker's Handbook by Bobby Harrington and Josh Robert Patrick; Discipleship Essentials by Greg Ogden; and The Master Plan of Evangelism by Robert Coleman.
